report.summary: Envelope chunk 3: canonical_sha, trace id functions, context management with fallback env propagation.
risks: canonical_sha | low | Uses canonical_json which is not defined in this chunk; if missing, will raise NameError. | Verify canonical_json is defined elsewhere in the module.
new_trace_id | low | Uses uuid.uuid4().hex[:8] which relies on random; collision probability is low but not zero. | Acceptable for practical uniqueness.

_scope | medium | Restores env variable to prior value or unsets it; if had_env is True but prior_env was empty string, restores empty string which may differ from absence. | Check if prior_env can be empty string and if that matters.

_scope | medium | When export_env is True and tid is None, always unsets env var even if parent had a different env value; but had_env check restores only if had_env was True. | Verify logic matches intended behavior for nested scopes.

handoff.purpose: Define canonical_sha, trace ID creation, context variable, and scope management functions.

symbols.name: canonical_sha
symbols.note: Returns hex digest of SHA256 over canonical JSON of object.

symbols.name: TRACE_KEY
symbols.note: String 'trace_id' – key for trace ID in records.

symbols.name: TRACE_ID_ENV
symbols.note: Environment variable name 'DAEDALUS_TRACE_ID' for cross-process propagation.

symbols.name: _TRACE_VAR
symbols.note: ContextVar for trace ID in current context.

symbols.name: new_trace_id
symbols.note: Generates a new trace ID string with timestamp and random hex.

symbols.name: current_trace_id
symbols.note: Returns current trace ID from context var or env, or None.

symbols.note: Binds trace ID to context var and returns reset token.

claims.text: sha256 over :func:`canonical_json` -- stable across insertion order.
claims.why: Canonical_json is not defined in this chunk; stability claim cannot be verified.

claims.text: Cross-PROCESS propagation. The file bus carries the trace inside the record for bridge hops (which is the standing rule -- no side channels), but a plain subprocess has no record to carry it in, so the environment is the only honest channel left.
claims.why: References file bus and bridge hops not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Read at :func:`current_trace_id` time rather than cached at import, so a parent that binds after import still propagates.
claims.why: current_trace_id reads from context var and env at call time, not cached.
Format matches f-string: tr- + timestamp + '-' + 8 hex chars.

claims.text: matching the house style already in ``loop.LoopDriver.run_id``
The stamp is for humans reading a directory listing; the uuid fragment is what makes it unique -- a collision needs two mints inside the same SECOND that also agree on 32 random bits.
claims.why: Timestamp has second precision; random part is 8 hex chars = 32 bits.

claims.text: The ``tr-`` prefix exists so a partial id is still recognisable in a grep hit.

Resolution order, and each step is a deliberate fallback: 1. the :class:`~contextvars.ContextVar` -- set by :func:`trace_context` in this process, correct under threads and async; 2. ``DAEDALUS_TRACE_ID`` -- set by a parent process, which is how a trace survives a ``subprocess`` boundary that carries no record.
claims.why: Function checks _TRACE_VAR.get() first, then env var TRACE_ID_ENV.

claims.text: This never mints. Auto-minting on a miss would be the worst possible behaviour...
claims.why: Function returns None if neither source has a value; no minting call.

claims.text: Prefer :func:`trace_context`. This is the escape hatch for a caller whose run does not fit a ``with`` block (a long-lived server binding per request).
claims.why: trace_context is defined later in this chunk but not fully shown; preference not verifiable.

claims.text: Restoration is unconditional and covers the exception path, because a leaked trace id is worse than no trace at all: it would silently glue the NEXT run's records onto this one's, producing a join that looks complete and is wrong.
claims.why: Finally block resets context var and restores env unconditionally.

claims.text: An untraced scope must UNSET it, not leave the parent's id behind for a child process to inherit and misattribute.
claims.why: When tid is None and export_env is True, os.environ.pop(TRACE_ID_ENV, None) is called.

claims.text: START a run. Mints an id when not given one; yields the id.
claims.why: In the shown code, if trace_id is None, new_trace_id() is called.

claims.text: This is the ONE place a trace is born: at the top of a run (a loop iteration, a wave, an offload, an ikarus ask).
claims.why: Claims about other call sites not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Nesting is honest -- an inner scope that passes no id gets a NEW id rather than silently adopting whatever happened to be in scope, because a fresh unlinked id is a visible hole while a silently reused one is a false join.
claims.why: When trace_id is None, new_trace_id() is called, ignoring current context.

claims.text: Use :func:`adopt_trace` instead when CONTINUING someone else's run. The two are separate functions rather than one flag because the difference matters and a boolean at the call site would not say which is meant: this one mints on ``None``, that one never mints.
claims.why: adopt_trace is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: ``export_env`` also sets ``DAEDALUS_TRACE_ID`` so children inherit it.
claims.why: The body of trace_context is truncated; export_env handling not shown.
